summary_en: Stem + -(으)ㅁ makes a noun; many results are fixed words (기쁨, 잠, 춤), and in notes and notices it ends a sentence as a terse statement (공사 중임).
ja_parallel: 連用形名詞（喜び・眠り・踊り）／体言止め
ja_diff_note: The fixed nouns line up neatly with 喜び, 悲しみ, 踊り. The memo/notice style (오늘 휴무임, 다 먹었음) has no exact Japanese form; it feels like 体言止め or a terse note. In ordinary speech, don't build new -(으)ㅁ nouns: use -는 것 or -기.
notes: Vowel stem + ㅁ, consonant stem + 음: 자다 -> 잠, 추다 -> 춤, 웃다 -> 웃음, 기쁘다 -> 기쁨, 슬프다 -> 슬픔. ㄹ stems take ㄻ: 살다 -> 삶.
Common fixed nouns: 잠 (sleep), 꿈 (dream), 춤 (dance), 웃음 (laughter), 걸음 (step), 기쁨 (joy), 슬픔 (sadness).
Notes and notices end in -(으)ㅁ, past -았/었음: 공사 중임, 오늘 휴무임, 확인했음. Texting uses it jokingly too (배고픔).
Rough split: -(으)ㅁ = written, states a fact; -기 = the action itself and set frames (하기 싫다); -는 것 = the all-purpose spoken choice.

examples.ko: 아빠는 텃밭에서 일하는 게 삶의 기쁨이래.
examples.en: Dad says working in the garden is the joy of his life.
examples.ja: お父さんは畑仕事が人生の喜びなんだって。

examples.ko: 엄마 오늘 늦음. 저녁은 냉장고에 있음.
examples.en: Mom's late today. Dinner's in the fridge.
examples.ja: 母、今日遅くなる。夕飯は冷蔵庫に。

drills.prompt_en: I couldn't fall asleep last night, so I'm tired.
drills.explain_en: 'Sleep won't come' is the set phrase 잠이 안 오다, using the noun 잠.
추다 takes its own noun 춤 as the object: 춤을 추다.
Memos end in -(으)ㅁ, with past -었음 for something already done.

drills.prompt_en: Ugh, I don't want to go to work.
drills.explain_en: The spoken frame 'don't want to' is -기 싫다; -(으)ㅁ doesn't fit it.
